title: The leftover after equal shares
hook: Ten objects among three people: where does the tenth go?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Preserve the remainder after dividing indivisible resources equally.

misconception: Equal whole-number shares distribute every object automatically.
objective: Preserve the remainder after dividing indivisible resources equally.

claims.text: Three recipients each receive the same whole-number count. Remainders are kept aside. Scaled model; whole objects; three equal shares.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Objects=10, A=9items and B=10items. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",3,["floor",["/","x",3]]]; B="x"; x denotes Objects. At x=10, A=9, B=10. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Floor division makes equal whole-number shares, but it can leave a remainder. Ten gives three each and one aside. A remainder has to stay in the inventory even when it cannot fit the equal-share rule.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",3,["floor",["/","x",3]]]; B="x"; x denotes Objects. At x=10, A=9, B=10. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Three recipients each get the same whole-number count; remainders stay aside. With 14 objects, how many stay aside? Correct: 2. Floor division gives four each (12 objects); the 2 left over stay in the inventory.
